title: Proactive Inference Ramp-up Orchestrator for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an orchestrator that proactively prepares dedicated GPU fleets for incoming inference traffic by coordinating model weight residency, staged KV cache priming, and controlled ramp-up to meet throughput guarantees while minimizing cold-start pain. This ticket covers the orchestration logic, autoscaling policy hooks, console controls, and metrics for SLO verification.
background: Customers running Dedicated capacity request predictable throughput and tight latency SLOs. Cold starts caused by unloaded model weights and empty KV caches lead to high tail latency and missed SLAs during scale-up and after deploys. Existing warm pool mechanisms partially address weight residency but lack coordinated KV priming and adaptive ramp policies tied to autoscaler signals and route-level throughput guarantees.
decision_summary: We will build a centralized Ramp-up Orchestrator service that subscribes to fleet lifecycle events and autoscaler signals, applies a policy graph to decide preloading actions, and emits explicit readiness states used by the routing layer to guarantee throughput. Key decisions: 1) keep model weight preloading in the runtime agent but drive it via orchestrator commands; 2) implement KV priming as staged replay of representative request prefixes (sample sets) rather than full traffic replay to bound cost; 3) expose conservative default policies but allow per-route overrides in Console.
implementation_notes:
- Orchestrator components: event consumer, policy evaluator, action planner, execution runner (RPC to runtime agents).
- Weight residency: introduce "residency_target" per model (percentage of nodes in fleet) and staged residency goals (30% -> 60% -> 100%) to support graceful ramp.
- KV priming: maintain per-model representative prefix set (seed prompts) derived from production traces (anonymized). Priming runs in parallel but rate-limited to avoid saturating GPUs.
- Autoscaler integration: orchestrator reads desired_capacity and scale_events; on upscales perform prioritized preloads to newly provisioned nodes.
- Routing handshake: new readiness flag (ramp_state) returned from runtime during health checks; router will only route production traffic to nodes at READY state or when fallback policy allows degraded capacity.
- Cost control: add budget cap and max-priming-rps parameters; priming respects token quota and can be throttled.
tradeoffs:
- Faster priming (larger parallelism) reduces cold-start latency but increases transient cost and can impact warm requests; we default to conservative parallelism.
- Representative prefix priming reduces cost versus full traffic replay but risks missing cold cache entries that appear only under rare queries; mitigations: periodic sampling and adaptive expansion of prefix sets.
- Staged residency increases time to absolute full capacity but provides smoother tail-latency behavior and fewer SLA violations during scale events.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start 95th pct latency reduction >= 50% for scale-up events on test fleets compared to baseline
Throughput guarantee: route-level P99 success rate meets SLA during controlled ramp tests (within configured residency targets)
Console exposes: residency_target, priming_budget_tokens, priming_parallelism, and per-route override toggles
New metrics: priming_tokens_used, priming_rps, residency_percent_by_model, ramp_state_transitions visible in Console time-series
End-to-end test and a canary rollout plan exist with rollback criteria
migrations_and_backward_compat: Runtime agent adds RPC handler for orchestrator commands but remains backward compatible: if orchestrator is not present, runtime falls back to current warm-pool behavior. Routing handshake is additive and defaults to existing health checks unless routes opt into ramp-based guarantees.
observability_plan:
- Create Grafana dashboards: priming budget burn-down, priming latency, residency attainment curve, cold-start tail latencies by fleet.
- Add tracing spans for orchestrator->runtime commands and priming sessions.
- Emit structured events for ramp_state transitions to the audit log for later incident analysis.
security_considerations: Priming uses anonymized prefix sets; access to prefix sets and orchestrator commands requires RBAC. Review required for KMS integration on clusters with HSM-backed keys. Audit logging enabled for all orchestrator actions.
tasks: Spec: detailed policy graph and default policy definitions (PM + Eng)
Runtime: add residency_target API and priming RPCs (ENG-impl-priming)
Orchestrator: implement event consumer and policy evaluator
Console: add UI controls for per-route warmup policy and budget caps
E2E: build test harness to simulate scale events and verify tail latency
Docs: runbook for on-call and cost monitoring during priming
